title: Mock Bananas and Acorn Coffee
hook: Boiled parsnips with banana essence fooled British kids.

scenes.text: During wartime rationing, exotic imported fruits completely vanished from British grocery store shelves for over five years.
scenes.imagePrompt: 1940s traditional wooden grocery storefront with empty wicker fruit crates in the window under soft morning light. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: During wartime rationing, exotic imported fruits completely vanished from British grocery store shelves for over five years.

scenes.text: Most children born during the war had never seen a real yellow banana, only hearing rumors of the mythical fruit from their parents.

scenes.voicedText: Most children born during the war had never seen a real yellow banana, only hearing rumors of the mythical fruit from their parents.

scenes.text: Clever mothers invented 'Mock Banana': boiling root parsnips until soft, mashing them with sugar and drops of artificial banana essence.

scenes.voicedText: Clever mothers invented 'Mock Banana': boiling root parsnips until soft, mashing them with sugar and drops of artificial banana essence.

scenes.text: Coffee lovers drank roasted chicory root or toasted roasted acorns ground into bitter brown powder.

scenes.text: Meanwhile, 'National Wheatmeal Bread' was heavy, grey, and legally banned from being sold until a day old to curb binge eating.
